title: Admin Synthesizer: Runbook->Task auditlet with provenance & telemetry shims
creator: Priya Narayanan
description: Build a lightweight 'auditlet' that converts authoring runbook snippets into discrete, verifiable tasks with an attached provenance header and pluggable telemetry shims. This ticket covers the core runtime adapter + schema, a guardrail for idempotent admin utilities, and a minimal operator UX hook so oncall engineers can inspect, approve, and replay generated task graphs. Goal is to make runbooks-as-tasks auditable, replayable, and observable with minimal changes for existing ops authors.
background: We have many ad-hoc runbook snippets and admin utilities used during incidents. Those are often executed manually, lack consistent telemetry, and miss action provenance (who triggered what, with which inputs). That makes post-incident analysis and quality gating for automated remediations difficult. The auditlet will bridge runbook fragments and the admin task runner by emitting a small envelope with action-hash, actor, trace_id, and idempotency token; it also wires in telemetry events for start/success/failure and resource-affecting deltas.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime adapter that accepts a runbook fragment and emits a task graph JSON with provenance header
2) Tasks include idempotency_token and action_hash fields and validate against a lightweight schema
3) Telemetry shim emits start/success/failure events to the ops-trace pipeline with trace_id linking
4) Operator UI shows the generated task graph with provenance and a review/approve button
5) End-to-end demo: author-runbook -> synthesize -> approve -> execute -> telemetry shows full lifecycle
implementation_notes: Implement adapter as a small Go microservice (ops-synth) that exposes an internal POST /synthesize endpoint. Use the existing runlet schema from ENG-314271 as the baseline, extend with new 'provenance' envelope. Idempotency token generation strategy: sha256(action_hash + actor + utc-date) truncated to 16 chars. Telemetry: reuse opstrace event format and attach trace_id propagated from incoming request. Safety: operations requiring elevated permissions must create a 'dry-run' preview by default; execution requires explicit operator approval via OAuth-backed console action. Include feature flag 'ops:auditlet' for staged rollout.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Choice: Go microservice to reuse platform infra vs. embedding in existing ops-runner. Decided on microservice for faster iteration and smaller blast radius.
Action provenance fields kept intentionally minimal to avoid PII in telemetry; any user-identifying data goes through hashed actor ids.
We will not attempt full automated remediation in this phase — aim is reliable synthesis + telemetry + UI review. Automation can be toggled in follow-up.
Schema versioning: add 'synth_version' field so dashboards can interpret older graphs during rollouts.

follow_up_tasks: Add automated regression tests that simulate duplicate submissions and verify idempotency
Create confluence runbook for migrating legacy snippets into the synth pipeline
Add metrics and SLO dashboard for synth service latencies and synth-to-execute success ratio
rollback_plan: Feature-flag the synth endpoint and gate UI approval behind 'ops:auditlet'. If telemetry or execution anomalies are observed, flip the flag off and queue synthetic events for reprocessing. Critical failures: rollback by redeploying previous synth image and restoring schema validation rules in the ops-runner.
security_considerations: Provenance headers will not include PII; actor identifiers are hashed. Any inputs flagged as 'secret' in runbook snippet metadata must be redacted before telemetry emission. Full security threat model added to Confluence link.
